target.title: fix(imessage): avoid surrogate pair truncation in replyToId sanitizer
target.body:
## Summary

Fix a low-severity Unicode truncation bug in the iMessage `sanitizeReplyToId` function. When a `replyToId` value exceeds the 256-character limit and contains non-BMP characters (emoji, CJK rare chars, etc.), `.slice(0, 256)` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing a dangling surrogate in the output.

**Root cause:** `extensions/imessage/src/send.ts:205` — `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, not code points. A non-BMP character encoded as a surrogate pair (2 code units) straddling position 256 produces an invalid string.

**Fix:** Replace `.slice(0, MAX_REPLY_TO_ID_LENGTH)` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which adjusts the cutoff boundary to avoid splitting surrogate pairs. This SDK utility is already used throughout the iMessage extension (cli-output.ts, coalesce.ts, monitor/connect.ts) for the same purpose.

## Evidence

### L2 verification — unit test output

All 47 send tests pass:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  47 passed (47)
```

### Reproduction (before vs after)

```javascript
// Before — dangling surrogate at slice boundary
const text = "a".repeat(255) + "\u{1F600}";  // 256 code units, emoji at boundary
text.slice(0, 256).charCodeAt(255).toString(16)  // → "d83d" (lone surrogate)

// After — truncateUtf16Safe preserves pair boundary
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from "@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice";
truncateUtf16Safe(text, 256).length  // → 255 (emoji excluded to keep pair intact)
```

### Before/after

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| ASCII at boundary | Correct | Correct (no change) |
| Non-BMP char at boundary | Dangling surrogate | Valid truncation |

## Design

Minimal change: single-function replacement. `truncateUtf16Safe` was chosen over `Array.from().slice().join()` because it is O(1) for the common ASCII-only case, is already a dependency in the extension, and matches the "truncate without breaking surrogate pairs" semantic exactly.

## What was not tested

- Actual iMessage CLI invocation with a non-BMP replyToId (requires physical macOS + Messages.app). Truncation verified at the unit level.

Ref. openclaw-fork-issue
